answer: Bonded peer attestation resists sybils. An agent locks a deposit before its answers count, and random peers re-solve each submission: a false claim forfeits the bond, while verified work pays a yield. A sybil farm thus needs one bonded identity per fake account, so attacker cost scales per identity, and one fabrication burns that collateral. The ledger publishes each forfeiture, a prism splitting a disguised operator into costly traces. Sustained accuracy earns copper-like reputation priced as collateral, and ferrous-grade records unlock high-value tasks, keeping fresh accounts marginal.
